scan_metadata.generator: Day 04 Social Engineering Awareness Engine v2.2

results.description: Voice phishing - attacker impersonates authority figure over phone

psychological_triggers.name: Authority
psychological_triggers.description: The scenario relies on an apparently trusted role or organization to increase perceived legitimacy.
psychological_triggers.example: Caller claims to be from IT Security Department
psychological_triggers.defense: Always verify identity through independent channels

psychological_triggers.name: Fear
psychological_triggers.description: The scenario introduces a possible negative consequence to encourage immediate action.
psychological_triggers.example: Your account will be permanently locked
psychological_triggers.defense: Stay calm and verify through official channels

psychological_triggers.name: Liking
psychological_triggers.description: The scenario uses friendliness, rapport, or common interests to increase trust.
psychological_triggers.example: Caller is friendly and 'helpful' to gain trust

script.phase_1_opener: Caller claims to be HR Representative from Sqrock IT. Uses professional tone to establish credibility.
script.phase_2_pretext: The caller explains: 'System Update Required' and states this requires immediate attention.
script.phase_3_hook: The scenario introduces an account or security concern designed to create urgency and fear.
script.phase_4_request: The simulated caller attempts to obtain sensitive information such as passwords, OTPs, or account details.
script.phase_5_pressure: If met with resistance, the caller increases urgency by threatening account suspension or security breaches.
script.awareness_note: This script demonstrates how vishing attacks use authority and fear to manipulate victims into sharing sensitive data.

red_flags.reason: A caller requesting passwords, authentication codes, or other secrets is a major warning sign.
Unsolicited calls about account problems should be independently verified.
Claiming to represent IT, security, a bank, or another trusted authority can be used to create false trust.
Pressure to act immediately can prevent the recipient from independently verifying the request.
Threatening account suspension, legal action, or other consequences is a common manipulation tactic.

defensive_guidance.detail: Never share passwords, authentication codes, or security questions over the phone.
End the call and contact the organization using official phone numbers from their website.
Caller ID can be spoofed to display any number the attacker chooses.
Legitimate organizations will not pressure you to make immediate decisions.
Report suspicious social-engineering attempts to your security team or IT department.

quiz.question: What type of social engineering attack is this?
quiz.explanation: This is a vishing attack because it uses voice call as the attack vector.

quiz.question: What is the primary psychological trigger being used?
quiz.explanation: The scenario relies on an apparently trusted role or organization to increase perceived legitimacy.

quiz.question: What is the BEST response to this scenario?
quiz.explanation: Always verify independently using official contact information, not information provided by the attacker.

results.description: SMS phishing - attacker sends malicious links via text

psychological_triggers.name: Authority
psychological_triggers.description: The scenario relies on an apparently trusted role or organization to increase perceived legitimacy.
psychological_triggers.example: Caller claims to be from IT Security Department
psychological_triggers.defense: Always verify identity through independent channels

psychological_triggers.name: Urgency
psychological_triggers.description: The scenario pressures the target to act quickly without thinking critically.
psychological_triggers.defense: Take a moment to pause and evaluate the request independently

psychological_triggers.name: Scarcity
psychological_triggers.description: The scenario presents a limited-time opportunity or consequence to create artificial value.
psychological_triggers.example: Only 2 hours left to verify your account
psychological_triggers.defense: Legitimate organizations don't use artificial deadlines

script.message_content: [Sqrock IT] ALERT: Suspicious Login Detected. Verify your account immediately: https://secure-login-verify.net/sqrock-it-suspicious-login-detected-a5eb10
script.pretext: The message claims that action is required because of: Suspicious Login Detected.
script.hook: The message uses urgency and fear to encourage the recipient to click the link without verification.
script.request: The link leads to a fake login page designed to steal credentials or install malware.
script.awareness_note: This demonstrates how smishing uses shortened URLs and urgency to trick victims into clicking malicious links.

red_flags.reason: Unexpected links in SMS messages should not be trusted without independent verification.
An unsolicited security or account notification should be verified through an official channel.
Threats of immediate account suspension can encourage impulsive clicking.
A message may claim to represent a trusted organization without actually originating from it.
Promises of prizes, refunds, or rewards are often used to entice victims to click malicious links.

defensive_guidance.detail: Never click links in unexpected SMS messages, even if they appear legitimate.
Check account status through the organization's official website or mobile application.
Replying confirms your number is active and may lead to more attacks.
Block the sender and report the message to your mobile carrier and security team.
Forward suspicious texts to 7726 (SPAM) in the US or your country's equivalent.

quiz.explanation: The scenario relies on an apparently trusted role or organization to increase perceived legitimacy.

quiz.question: What is the BEST response to this scenario?
quiz.explanation: Always verify independently using official contact information, not information provided by the attacker.
